status_summary: DOT issued a tentative decision on 2025-10-09 that would bar seven Chinese carriers from using Russian airspace on scheduled passenger and combination flights between China and the U.S., taking effect 30 days after a final order; all-cargo services were tentatively left unconditioned. Trade reporting of 2025-10-20 said three carriers filed comments opposing the proposed order and that DOT rejected a request for more time from the other covered carriers. No final order was found.

timeline.event: DOT issued a tentative decision to bar seven Chinese carriers from Russian airspace on passenger flights to and from the U.S., to take effect 30 days after a final order.

title: Deny foreign carriers a Russian overflight advantage on U.S. routes; hold China talks
uncertainties: The DOT order itself was not located or opened; it is known from trade reports (ch-aviation, Air Cargo News) and a law firm update, which differ on whether it is a tentative decision or an order to show cause, and none gives a docket number. The ch-aviation report of 2025-10-20 was reread on 2026-10-18; it names Capital Airlines among the covered carriers, while another trade report read by the researcher lists Beijing Airlines, so the carrier list is not settled. A Federal Register API term search found no related document, and DOT orders under air services agreements are docketed outside the Federal Register, so a final order could exist that these checks did not surface. One web search on 2026-10-18 for a final order returned only October 2025 reports of the proposal. transportation.gov could not be reached for a release on the topic. The Mandate covers carriers serving East and South Asia generally, while the action names only Chinese carriers. No step on withholding new negotiations with China was found.
